text:
No causal–interventional knowledge fabric can be extracted from the supplied “data source” because the material provided is only a bibliography (a list of citations) rather than the substantive body of a paper that describes:

• the risks or problems being addressed  
• the theoretical or empirical methods used  
• the findings or conclusions drawn  
• the interventions or recommendations proposed  

All of these elements are required to identify and connect nodes along the mandatory pathway
Risk → Problem Analysis → Theoretical Insight → Design Rationale → Implementation Mechanism → Validation Evidence → Intervention.

A bibliography, by definition, contains none of this explanatory content; it merely points to other documents that might contain such content. Because:

1. No risks are stated or even hinted at.  
2. No analytical narrative or method descriptions appear.  
3. No experimental or observational results are given.  
4. No proposed solutions or interventions are presented.  

…it is impossible to create any nodes (let alone a connected fabric) without inventing unsupported content, which would violate the instruction to avoid speculative fabrication and to assign appropriate evidence-strength scores.

Therefore, the knowledge-fabric extraction task is infeasible on this input.

Recommendations for enabling successful extraction in future:

1. Provide the complete article text, including abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, and any conclusions or recommendations.  
2. Ensure that at least one explicit problem statement and one proposed solution or intervention appear; otherwise, the mandated node categories cannot be populated.  
3. When only bibliographic metadata is available, clarify that the task is instead to map potential sources for future extraction, or postpone extraction until full texts are accessible.

These steps will supply the necessary causal and interventional information to meet the mandatory success criteria.
